class: DataFrames whose selected column contains string categories first encountered in an order different from lexicographic order.
rule_a: String categories in the selected column must receive consecutive integer codes starting at zero in order of first appearance, with repeated categories receiving the same code.
rule_b: String categories in the selected column must receive consecutive integer codes starting at zero in lexicographic order, with repeated categories receiving the same code.

class: JSON responses whose ip value encodes a valid IPv4 address using JSON Unicode escapes for digits or periods.
rule_a: When the ip value contains JSON Unicode escapes for digits or periods, validate its literal escaped spelling and return 'Invalid IP address received' if that spelling is not an IPv4 address.
rule_b: When the ip value contains JSON Unicode escapes for digits or periods, validate its decoded spelling and return the decoded address if that spelling is an IPv4 address.

class: DataFrames whose replacement dictionary includes numeric cell values as keys.
rule_a: When the dictionary includes numeric cell values as keys, leave numeric cells unchanged, replace matching categorical values, and calculate the Pearson correlation matrix.
rule_b: When the dictionary includes numeric cell values as keys, replace matching numeric and categorical values with their dictionary values, and calculate the Pearson correlation matrix.

class: DataFrames containing multiple id groups whose means differ in at least one of the age and income columns.
rule_a: Standardization must center and scale each of the age and income columns using that column's mean and population standard deviation across the entire DataFrame.
rule_b: Standardization must center and scale each of the age and income columns using that column's mean and population standard deviation within each row's id group.

class: Positive decimal values supplied with default precision whose square roots have a third fractional digit from 5 through 9 and at least one later nonzero digit.
rule_a: When precision is omitted, the square root must be truncated to two decimal places before its decimal string representation is JSON-encoded.
rule_b: When precision is omitted, the square root must be rounded to the nearest hundredth before its decimal string representation is JSON-encoded.

class: Tuples containing repeated numeric values, with subset_size equal to 2.
rule_a: For a tuple containing repeated values and subset_size equal to 2, remove duplicate values before forming all unordered pairs and counting their sums.
rule_b: For a tuple containing repeated values and subset_size equal to 2, form all unordered pairs of distinct tuple positions and count their sums, preserving the multiplicity of repeated values.

class: Nonempty rectangular lists of numeric rows containing at least one non-integral float.
rule_a: For inputs containing non-integral floats, values must be truncated toward zero to integers before constructing the DataFrame and calculating Euclidean distances between rows.
rule_b: For inputs containing non-integral floats, values must retain their fractional parts when constructing the DataFrame and calculating Euclidean distances between rows.

class: The pattern is empty and the specified column contains strings with at least two distinct whitespace-separated words.
rule_a: When the pattern is empty, return a new DataFrame with every string in the specified column's word order reversed, joining words with single spaces and leaving all other data unchanged.
rule_b: When the pattern is empty, return a new DataFrame with every string in the specified column preserved exactly, including its word order and whitespace, and leave all other data unchanged.

class: Nested dictionaries in which at least one key other than "ele" has an aggregate sum of zero or less.
rule_a: Sum the values for each key across the inner dictionaries, remove "ele" and any keys whose sums are nonpositive, and return the sine of each retained sum.
rule_b: Sum the values for each key across the inner dictionaries, remove only "ele" while retaining keys whose sums are nonpositive, and return the sine of each retained sum.

class: Lists of lists in which at least one element occurs more than once within a single sublist.
rule_a: Return a collections.Counter counting each element once per sublist containing it, regardless of repeated occurrences within that sublist.
rule_b: Return a collections.Counter counting every occurrence of each element in every sublist, including repeated occurrences within the same sublist.

class: Numeric DataFrames containing at least one column whose entries are all the same nonzero value.
rule_a: Constant columns must retain their original values, while nonconstant columns must be centered and divided by their population standard deviations.
rule_b: Constant columns must become zero-valued columns, while nonconstant columns must be centered and divided by their population standard deviations.

class: Finite two-dimensional NumPy arrays with at least two columns whose population standard deviations are positive and unequal.
rule_a: Return a DataFrame preserving the input's shape and order, subtracting each column's mean and dividing every centered value by the single population standard deviation of all centered entries pooled together.
rule_b: Return a DataFrame preserving the input's shape and order, subtracting each column's mean and dividing every centered value by the population standard deviation of its own column.

class: Numeric DataFrames containing both integer-typed and floating-point-typed columns.
rule_a: For DataFrames containing integer-typed and floating-point-typed columns, return Shapiro-Wilk p-values keyed by column label for only the floating-point columns, excluding integer columns as discrete data.
rule_b: For DataFrames containing integer-typed and floating-point-typed columns, return Shapiro-Wilk p-values keyed by column label for every column, including integer columns as numeric data.

class: Nested numeric lists whose nonempty inner lists have unequal lengths.
rule_a: For unequal-length nonempty inner lists, calculate the mean and population variance by giving each inner list equal total weight, divided equally among its elements.
rule_b: For unequal-length nonempty inner lists, calculate the mean and population variance by giving every element equal weight, regardless of which inner list contains it.

class: Datasets consisting of exactly two points whose Euclidean distance is exactly 3.
rule_a: For exactly two points at Euclidean distance 3, the returned DataFrame must assign Cluster=-1 to both rows because the eps neighborhood excludes its boundary.
rule_b: For exactly two points at Euclidean distance 3, the returned DataFrame must assign Cluster=0 to both rows because the eps neighborhood includes its boundary.

class: Numeric DataFrames in which the column named by target is not the last column.
rule_a: When the named target column is not last, the returned R-squared must describe regression predicting the last column using the remaining columns as predictors.
rule_b: When the named target column is not last, the returned R-squared must describe regression predicting the named target column using the remaining columns as predictors.

class: Dictionaries with nonempty string keys in which some initial letters occur in both uppercase and lowercase.
rule_a: For these dictionaries, entries must be grouped by their first character converted to lowercase, with each group's values summed under that lowercase character.
rule_b: For these dictionaries, entries must be grouped by their first character exactly as written, with each group's values summed under that unchanged character.

class: Nonempty lists of category-value tuples containing repeated category labels and finite numeric values.
rule_a: When category labels repeat, the returned DataFrame must contain one row per distinct category in first-appearance order, with category means normalized together using MinMaxScaler.
rule_b: When category labels repeat, the returned DataFrame must contain one row per input tuple in input order, with the original tuple values normalized together using MinMaxScaler.

class: Nonconstant numeric lists whose values are not in nondecreasing order.
rule_a: For a nonconstant numeric list that is not in nondecreasing order, return an ndarray containing each value scaled as (value − minimum)/(maximum − minimum), arranged in ascending order.
rule_b: For a nonconstant numeric list that is not in nondecreasing order, return an ndarray containing each value scaled as (value − minimum)/(maximum − minimum), arranged in the original input order.

class: Comma-separated strings in which at least one nonnegative integer or decimal entry occurs more than once.
rule_a: Repeated numeric entries must contribute only once per distinct numeric value to both the count and the sum of square roots.
rule_b: Repeated numeric entries must contribute once per occurrence to both the count and the sum of square roots.

class: Lists of uppercase letters containing at least one repeated letter.
rule_a: For a list containing repeated letters, the function must multiply the corresponding alphabet positions of each distinct letter exactly once.
rule_b: For a list containing repeated letters, the function must multiply the corresponding alphabet positions of every letter occurrence, including repetitions.

class: Inputs containing inner lists with more than ten elements.
rule_a: For each inner list longer than ten elements, its output must be the sum of the squares of consecutive integers from 1 through that list's length, ignoring its element values.
rule_b: For each inner list longer than ten elements, its output must be the sum of the squares of the available integers from 1 through 10, ignoring its element values.

class: Nested lists containing repeated menu items within an inner list, with a unique winner both by total occurrence count and by number of inner lists containing the item.
rule_a: For these inputs, count each menu item at most once per inner list and return the item with the highest count.
rule_b: For these inputs, count every occurrence of each menu item across all inner lists and return the item with the highest count.

class: Texts containing at least one whitespace-separated substring composed entirely of ASCII punctuation.
rule_a: Each whitespace-separated substring composed entirely of ASCII punctuation must contribute zero words, zero characters, and zero unique characters to the counts.
rule_b: Each whitespace-separated substring composed entirely of ASCII punctuation must contribute one word, zero characters, and zero unique characters to the counts.

class: Inputs containing only numeric columns where the requested columns are a nonempty proper subset of the dictionary's columns.
rule_a: When only some numeric columns are requested, return all columns with every column independently min-max scaled to the range from 0 to 1.
rule_b: When only some numeric columns are requested, return all columns with only the requested columns independently min-max scaled to the range from 0 to 1 and all other columns unchanged.

class: Text containing the standalone words 'no', 'nor', or 'not', which are absent from the predefined stopword set.
class_inputs: ('we are not going to the park',)
other_inputs: ('Visit https://www.python.org for more info. I love to eat apples.',)
rule_a: The standalone words 'no', 'nor', and 'not' must be removed as common English stopwords when cleaning the text.
rule_b: The standalone words 'no', 'nor', and 'not' must be retained because they are absent from the predefined stopword set.

class: Dictionaries containing lowercase names of real animals that are absent from ANIMAL.
rule_a: Real animal names absent from ANIMAL must contribute their letters to the returned frequencies alongside names present in ANIMAL, with frequencies sorted in descending order.
rule_b: Real animal names absent from ANIMAL must contribute no letters to the returned frequencies, which must count only names present in ANIMAL and be sorted in descending order.

class: Two-dimensional numeric arrays with zero elements because at least one dimension is zero.
rule_a: For an input with zero elements, the result must contain an empty array retaining the input's two-dimensional shape and an empty list of pairs.
rule_b: For an input with zero elements, the result must contain a one-dimensional empty array of shape (0,) and an empty list of pairs.

class: Nonempty lists containing multiple tuples with the same category.
rule_a: For lists with repeated categories, return a single-element 1D numeric array containing the product of the second values after keeping only the last tuple for each category.
rule_b: For lists with repeated categories, return a single-element 1D numeric array containing the product of the second values of every tuple, including all tuples sharing a category.

class: Two nonempty numeric lists of unequal lengths, using the default threshold, with a unique closest element both overall and among the paired elements.
rule_a: For these inputs, return the element closest to 0.5 among only the paired elements, discarding the unmatched tail of the longer list.
rule_b: For these inputs, return the element closest to 0.5 among all existing elements, including the unmatched tail of the longer list.

class: Dictionaries whose value lists contain at least one negative integer.
rule_a: For dictionaries containing negative integers, return the occurrence counts of all nonnegative integers across all lists, omitting negative integers.
rule_b: For dictionaries containing negative integers, return the occurrence counts of all integers across all lists, including negative integers.

class: Texts containing at least one nonempty sentence composed entirely of lowercase words from STOPWORDS.
class_inputs: ('Birds sing. words to ignore. Rain falls.',)
rule_a: A nonempty sentence composed entirely of lowercase words from STOPWORDS must be omitted from the returned Series.
rule_b: A nonempty sentence composed entirely of lowercase words from STOPWORDS must be included in the returned Series with a word count of zero.

class: Lists of positive integers containing repeated values.
rule_a: For lists containing repeated positive integers, duplicate occurrences must be removed before summing the natural logarithms of the products of all nonempty combinations.
rule_b: For lists containing repeated positive integers, duplicate occurrences must be retained as distinct selectable entries when summing the natural logarithms of the products of all nonempty combinations.

class: Nonempty DataFrames with distinct column labels that are an unsorted permutation of consecutive integers starting at zero.
rule_a: For these DataFrames, the function must return the skewness of the column whose integer label is largest.
rule_b: For these DataFrames, the function must return the skewness of the column whose position is last.

class: Lists containing at least one string with leading or trailing whitespace.
rule_a: For strings with leading or trailing whitespace, Count must equal the number of characters remaining after stripping that whitespace, while Element must retain the original string.
rule_b: For strings with leading or trailing whitespace, Count must equal the number of characters in the entire string including that whitespace, while Element must retain the original string.

class: The target and all dataset points lie on the equator, with at least one point differing from the target by more than 180 degrees in longitude.
rule_a: For these inputs, return the k nearest points in ascending order of the absolute, unwrapped longitude difference from the target.
rule_b: For these inputs, return the k nearest points in ascending order of the shortest longitude separation from the target around the globe.

class: Lists of string categories whose distinct values first appear in an order different from lexicographic order.
rule_a: For string categories, assign consecutive integer codes starting at zero in order of first appearance, preserving every original value and its row position.
rule_b: For string categories, assign consecutive integer codes starting at zero in lexicographic order of distinct values, preserving every original value and its row position.

class: JSON strings containing multiple datetime-valued fields, including 'utc_datetime', whose dates may fall on different days of the week.
rule_a: For JSON strings containing multiple datetime-valued fields, return True exactly when the datetime in the first field falls on Saturday or Sunday.
rule_b: For JSON strings containing multiple datetime-valued fields, return True exactly when the datetime in the 'utc_datetime' field falls on Saturday or Sunday.

class: Inputs where at least one text row contains multiple occurrences of a word that survives preprocessing.
rule_a: For each text row, each surviving word's output column must contain 1 if that word occurs in the row and 0 otherwise.
rule_b: For each text row, each surviving word's output column must contain the number of times that word occurs in the row, including 0 when absent.

class: JSON dictionaries containing URL-valued strings inside nested dictionaries.
rule_a: For JSON dictionaries containing nested dictionaries, URL-valued strings must contribute to occurrence counts only when they are direct values of the outermost dictionary.
rule_b: For JSON dictionaries containing nested dictionaries, URL-valued strings must contribute to occurrence counts whether they are direct values of the outermost dictionary or of any nested dictionary.

class: Integer upper bounds less than 1, for which the range contains no eligible numbers.
rule_a: For an integer n less than 1, the function must return an empty list.
rule_b: For an integer n less than 1, the function must raise ValueError.

class: Nonempty DataFrames with repeated customer names whose repeated rows have identical category and sales values, and a unique most frequent category both before and after deduplication.
rule_a: For these inputs, the report must sum sales once per customer and determine the most popular category by counting every original row.
rule_b: For these inputs, the report must sum sales once per customer and determine the most popular category by counting each customer once.

class: Tuples of distinct positive integers for which different subsets of the requested size have equal sums.
rule_a: When different subsets have equal sums, each distinct sum must contribute exactly once to the product and exactly once to the descending sequence used to select the top_n sums.
rule_b: When different subsets have equal sums, each subset's sum must contribute separately to the product and separately to the descending sequence used to select the top_n sums.

class: Inputs containing a nonempty number list with r equal to zero.
rule_a: When the number list is nonempty and r is zero, the function must return an empty list.
rule_b: When the number list is nonempty and r is zero, the function must return a list containing exactly one empty tuple.

class: Columns containing both numbers and numeric strings, with every value convertible to a finite float.
rule_a: A column containing both numbers and numeric strings, with every value convertible to a finite float, must remain unchanged.
rule_b: A column containing both numbers and numeric strings, with every value convertible to a finite float, must be converted to numeric values and scaled using StandardScaler.

class: Nonconstant one-dimensional NumPy arrays whose values are not in ascending order.
rule_a: Return a DataFrame with column 'Scaled Values' containing (x - min(l)) / (max(l) - min(l)) for every input element, arranged in ascending value order.
rule_b: Return a DataFrame with column 'Scaled Values' containing (x - min(l)) / (max(l) - min(l)) for every input element, retaining the original input order.

class: Single-line strings containing nonnested square-bracketed spans followed by unbracketed words after the final closing bracket.
class_inputs: ('quiet river [discard these words] bright meadow bright',)
rule_a: For such strings, the TF-IDF dictionary must be calculated from all unbracketed text preceding the final closing bracket, excluding the trailing unbracketed words.
rule_b: For such strings, the TF-IDF dictionary must be calculated from all unbracketed text preceding the final closing bracket together with the trailing unbracketed words.

class: Nonempty JSON dictionaries whose values are all numerical scalars rather than lists.
rule_a: For a nonempty JSON dictionary containing only numerical scalars, the function must return an empty DataFrame because there are no lists to define its rows.
rule_b: For a nonempty JSON dictionary containing only numerical scalars, the function must return a one-row DataFrame with one column per key and every value doubled.

class: The input object is a Python string whose contents are valid JSON text.
rule_a: When the input is a Python string containing valid JSON text, return its contents unchanged as the serialized result.
rule_b: When the input is a Python string containing valid JSON text, encode the entire string as a JSON string value, adding surrounding double quotes and escaping its contents as required.

class: Lists containing at least one empty string or string consisting entirely of whitespace.
rule_a: After lowercasing and trimming each string, omit strings that become empty and count the remaining strings in the Count column.
rule_b: After lowercasing and trimming each string, retain strings that become empty and count them under the empty-string index in the Count column.

class: Compatible nonempty inputs whose flattened multiplication result contains at least one feature with a constant nonzero value across all rows.
rule_a: Normalization must leave each constant nonzero feature at its original value and apply StandardScaler to all remaining features.
rule_b: Normalization must replace each constant nonzero feature with zeros and apply StandardScaler to all remaining features.

class: Dictionaries and lists containing a nonempty Python set as a value or element.
rule_a: When a dictionary or list contains a Python set, serialization must encode the set's Python string representation as a JSON string value.
rule_b: When a dictionary or list contains a Python set, serialization must raise TypeError because the set is an unsupported type.

class: Nested menu lists in which at least one menu item appears multiple times within the same inner list.
rule_a: For these inputs, each menu item's 'Count' must equal the number of inner lists containing that item.
rule_b: For these inputs, each menu item's 'Count' must equal the total number of occurrences of that item across all inner lists.

class: Nonempty stock data containing repeated identical daily records and selecting a numeric column.
rule_a: For repeated identical daily records, the selected numeric column's sum, mean, minimum, and maximum must count each distinct daily record exactly once.
rule_b: For repeated identical daily records, the selected numeric column's sum, mean, minimum, and maximum must count every listed occurrence of each daily record.

class: Inputs with a lowercase filtering letter and both words starting with that letter and words containing it only at later positions.
rule_a: Compute the mean, median, and mode of the lengths of all words containing the specified letter anywhere.
rule_b: Compute the mean, median, and mode of the lengths of all words starting with the specified letter.

class: Two nonempty 2D numeric NumPy arrays have equal row counts but unequal column counts.
rule_a: For matrices with equal row counts but unequal column counts, the function must raise ValueError because joining the matrices requires matching column counts.
rule_b: For matrices with equal row counts but unequal column counts, the function must append all columns of the second matrix after all columns of the first and return the resulting DataFrame as a string without index or header.

class: DataFrames processed with the default pattern that contain cells with exactly one matching numeric substring surrounded by additional text.
rule_a: When using the default pattern, a cell containing exactly one matching numeric substring and additional text must be replaced with NaN.
rule_b: When using the default pattern, a cell containing exactly one matching numeric substring and additional text must be replaced with the numeric value extracted from that substring.

class: Strings with strictly positive character weights whose occurrences are not already grouped in dictionary insertion order.
rule_a: For strings with strictly positive character weights, return every character occurrence grouped by character in dictionary insertion order.
rule_b: For strings with strictly positive character weights, return every character occurrence in its original order in the input string.

class: Dictionaries with a frequency tie that crosses the cutoff for a positive number n of requested letters.
rule_a: When a frequency tie crosses the nth-letter cutoff, return every letter above the cutoff and every letter tied at the cutoff, even if this yields more than n letters.
rule_b: When a frequency tie crosses the nth-letter cutoff, return every letter above the cutoff and only enough letters tied at the cutoff to yield exactly n letters.

class: Dictionaries with nonzero lengths and negative-valued entries separated by positive-valued entries.
rule_a: For a nonempty dictionary, return the keys in insertion order of a nonempty contiguous block having the minimum total value, without skipping intervening entries.
rule_b: For a nonempty dictionary, return the keys in insertion order of a nonempty subsequence having the minimum total value, allowing intervening entries to be skipped.

class: Strings containing repeated characters, with a specified weight for every character.
rule_a: For strings containing repeated characters, each candidate substring must count each distinct character's weight once, and the returned substring must maximize that sum.
rule_b: For strings containing repeated characters, each candidate substring must count every occurrence of each character's weight, and the returned substring must maximize that sum.

class: Input DataFrames contain additional columns besides 'var1' and 'var2', with no existing 'predicted' column.
rule_a: For DataFrames containing additional columns, the returned DataFrame must discard those columns and contain only 'var1', 'var2', and the newly computed 'predicted' column.
rule_b: For DataFrames containing additional columns, the returned DataFrame must preserve those columns and their values alongside 'var1', 'var2', and the newly computed 'predicted' column.

class: Dictionaries with at least three distinct nonnegative values, at least one exceeding π, and distinct individual cosine values.
rule_a: The returned pair must contain the keys whose values are the two numerically smallest values in the dictionary.
rule_b: The returned pair must contain the keys whose values have the two largest individual cosines in the dictionary.

class: DataFrames containing rows with the same multiset of items arranged in different column positions.
rule_a: Rows containing the same multiset of items in different column positions must be counted as separate combinations for each distinct item1-through-item5 sequence.
rule_b: Rows containing the same multiset of items in different column positions must be counted together as occurrences of a single combination.

class: DataFrames with a default zero-based index that already contain a boolean 'IsEvenIndex' column and have a different column selected for removal.
rule_a: When removing a different column from a DataFrame with a default zero-based index, an existing 'IsEvenIndex' column must retain its current boolean values.
rule_b: When removing a different column from a DataFrame with a default zero-based index, an existing 'IsEvenIndex' column must receive boolean values indicating whether each row's index is even.

class: Inputs containing nonempty integer lists of unequal lengths.
rule_a: When the inner lists have unequal lengths, compute the mode and its frequency using only the first k elements of each inner list, where k is the shortest inner-list length.
rule_b: When the inner lists have unequal lengths, compute the mode and its frequency using every element of every inner list.

class: Nonempty lists of nonempty numeric tuples whose lengths differ.
rule_a: For tuples of unequal lengths, the DataFrame must preserve tuple order as rows and apply math.sin only to positions present in every tuple, discarding trailing values beyond the shortest tuple.
rule_b: For tuples of unequal lengths, the DataFrame must preserve tuple order as rows and apply math.sin to every supplied value, filling missing positions through the longest tuple with NaN.

class: Dataframes containing additional numeric columns besides the named 'feature' and 'value' columns.
rule_a: When additional numeric columns are present, fit 'value' using every column except 'value' as predictors in dataframe column order, and return the fitted coefficients and intercept.
rule_b: When additional numeric columns are present, fit 'value' using only the named 'feature' column as the predictor, and return the fitted coefficients and intercept.

class: Numeric data containing at least one column whose value is constant across two or more rows.
rule_a: Constant numeric columns must be omitted from both axes of the correlation matrix, leaving only the remaining numeric columns.
rule_b: Constant numeric columns must be retained on both axes of the correlation matrix, with every entry involving them set to NaN.

class: Numeric DataFrames with exactly two feature columns, for which PCA preserves the number of columns but can change their values.
rule_a: For a numeric DataFrame with exactly two columns, the output must preserve the original feature values in their existing column order and name the columns 'PC1' and 'PC2'.
rule_b: For a numeric DataFrame with exactly two columns, the output must contain the fitted, centered PCA scores in descending explained-variance order and name the columns 'PC1' and 'PC2'.

class: Numeric tuple lists in which at least one column's arithmetic mean differs from the midpoint of its minimum and maximum.
rule_a: Compute the requested principal-component scores by applying SVD after centering each column at the midpoint of its minimum and maximum.
rule_b: Compute the requested principal-component scores by applying SVD after centering each column at its arithmetic mean.

class: Inputs containing at least one pair of nonconstant columns whose absolute correlation exactly equals the supplied threshold.
rule_a: A pair of columns whose absolute correlation exactly equals the supplied threshold must be included in the returned combinations.
rule_b: A pair of columns whose absolute correlation exactly equals the supplied threshold must be excluded from the returned combinations.

class: Strings consisting of whitespace-separated lowercase words of at least two letters, with at least one word repeated.
rule_a: For these strings, each vocabulary attribute must contain 1 if its word appears in the input and 0 if it does not.
rule_b: For these strings, each vocabulary attribute must contain its word's total occurrence count in the input and 0 if it does not appear.

class: DataFrames with multiple numeric columns, where the named column is only one of them.
rule_a: For a DataFrame with multiple numeric columns, the function must return whether all numeric values pooled across those columns pass the Shapiro-Wilk normality test at the supplied significance level.
rule_b: For a DataFrame with multiple numeric columns, the function must return whether the values in the named column alone pass the Shapiro-Wilk normality test at the supplied significance level.

class: Pairs of strings consisting of alphabetic words separated by single spaces, with unequal word counts and at least three words in each string.
class_inputs: ('one three seven', 'a bb ccc dddd eeeee')
('a bb ccc dddd eeeee', 'one three seven')
rule_a: For these strings, the function must equalize the word counts by discarding trailing words from the longer word sequence, then return the paired t-test statistic and p-value for the remaining word lengths.
rule_b: For these strings, the function must return (NaN, NaN) because their word counts differ, without discarding trailing words to make a paired t-test possible.

class: Nested lists consisting of nonempty numeric sublists with unequal lengths.
rule_a: For nested lists with unequal sublist lengths, return the median of the sublist medians, giving each sublist equal weight.
rule_b: For nested lists with unequal sublist lengths, return the median of all individual numeric elements, giving each element equal weight.

class: Sentences ending in a stop word and containing at least one preceding non-stop word.
rule_a: For a sentence ending in a stop word, remove all stop words and then omit the last remaining word before counting.
rule_b: For a sentence ending in a stop word, omit the sentence's last word and then remove all stop words before counting.

class: Rectangular nested lists of finite numbers in which some values occur more than once.
rule_a: For nested lists containing repeated values, calculate the interquartile range across the distinct numeric values, counting each value only once.
rule_b: For nested lists containing repeated values, calculate the interquartile range across all numeric elements, counting every occurrence of each value.

class: JSON objects containing at least one zero, false, or empty-string value.
rule_a: Entries whose values are zero, false, or empty strings must be removed along with null-valued entries before email replacement and frequency counting.
rule_b: Entries whose values are zero, false, or empty strings must be retained while null-valued entries are removed before email replacement and frequency counting.

class: Inputs with a nonempty list of distinct alphabetic patterns, at least one of which does not occur in the string.
rule_a: When any supplied pattern is absent from the string, the returned dictionary must include occurring patterns with their counts and omit absent patterns.
rule_b: When any supplied pattern is absent from the string, the returned dictionary must include occurring patterns with their counts and absent patterns with a count of zero.

class: Strings containing at least one uppercase ASCII letter before their final hyphen.
rule_a: For strings containing uppercase ASCII letters before their final hyphen, return a dictionary counting all 26 lowercase ASCII letters in that prefix, converting uppercase ASCII letters to lowercase before counting.
rule_b: For strings containing uppercase ASCII letters before their final hyphen, return a dictionary counting all 26 lowercase ASCII letters in that prefix, ignoring uppercase ASCII letters when counting.

class: Dictionaries containing uppercase letter keys and at least three lowercase letter keys, with distinct positive integer counts.
rule_a: For these dictionaries, return the three letter keys with the highest counts in descending count order, considering only lowercase keys.
rule_b: For these dictionaries, return the three letter keys with the highest counts in descending count order, considering all letter keys.

class: Input lists containing exactly two elements, for which a three-position rotation wraps around the list.
rule_a: For a two-element input list, the returned deque must contain the elements in their original order.
rule_b: For a two-element input list, the returned deque must contain the elements in reversed order.

class: Equal-length one-dimensional arrays containing at least three elements, with corresponding elements defining an ordered sequence of points.
rule_a: For arrays containing at least three elements, the function must return the maximum Euclidean distance between points at consecutive corresponding indices.
rule_b: For arrays containing at least three elements, the function must return the maximum Euclidean distance between points at any two distinct corresponding indices.

class: Lists containing repeated numeric values where at least one matching three-number combination uses a value more than once.
rule_a: For lists containing repeated numeric values, the dataframe must contain all unique combinations summing to the target that use three pairwise distinct numeric values.
rule_b: For lists containing repeated numeric values, the dataframe must contain all unique combinations summing to the target that use three distinct list positions, allowing equal numeric values.

class: Strings containing apostrophes or hyphens between letters within a whitespace-delimited word.
rule_a: An apostrophe or hyphen between letters must split the surrounding text into separate lowercase words.
rule_b: An apostrophe or hyphen between letters must be deleted, joining the surrounding letters into one lowercase word.

class: Two-dimensional arrays with rows out of lexicographic order, so sorting can change the indices associated with cluster members.
rule_a: For arrays with rows out of lexicographic order, each cluster must contain the zero-based row indices of its members in a lexicographically sorted copy of the input array.
rule_b: For arrays with rows out of lexicographic order, each cluster must contain the zero-based row indices of its members in the original input array.

class: Strings containing consecutive punctuation characters from PUNCTUATION.
rule_a: For strings containing consecutive punctuation characters, the punctuation total must count each maximal contiguous run of characters from PUNCTUATION as one mark.
rule_b: For strings containing consecutive punctuation characters, the punctuation total must count each individual character from PUNCTUATION as one mark.

class: JSON strings whose text field contains ASCII punctuation directly between letters or digits within a token.
rule_a: When ASCII punctuation occurs between letters or digits, replace it with a word boundary before counting the resulting lowercase words.
rule_b: When ASCII punctuation occurs between letters or digits, delete it without introducing a word boundary before counting the resulting lowercase words.

class: Nonempty lists of nonnegative integers containing repeated values.
rule_a: For lists containing repeated values, return each distinct value permutation once, with one corresponding sum of factorials for each returned permutation.
rule_b: For lists containing repeated values, return every positional permutation including duplicate value permutations, with one corresponding sum of factorials for each returned permutation.

class: Nonempty lists in which at least one fruit appears multiple times and has a non-integer arithmetic mean count.
rule_a: For each fruit, 'Total Count' must sum all its counts and 'Average Count' must divide that sum by the number of its tuples using integer floor division.
rule_b: For each fruit, 'Total Count' must sum all its counts and 'Average Count' must divide that sum by the number of its tuples without rounding to an integer.

class: Inputs where at least one string contains an ASCII hyphen directly between two ASCII letters or digits.
rule_a: Each ASCII hyphen directly between two ASCII letters or digits must be replaced with a single space, all other ASCII punctuation must be deleted, and every remaining character must be preserved.
rule_b: Each ASCII hyphen directly between two ASCII letters or digits must be deleted without replacement, all other ASCII punctuation must be deleted, and every remaining character must be preserved.

class: Nonempty single-line strings with leading spaces, where those spaces and the first word together fit within the requested width.
rule_a: Leading spaces must be excluded when measuring the first wrapped line against the specified width.
rule_b: Leading spaces must be included when measuring the first wrapped line against the specified width.

class: Nonempty lists containing tuples of unequal lengths.
rule_a: For tuples of unequal lengths, return a 'Mean Value' row labelled 'Position i' for each position present in every tuple, averaging only available numeric values and using NaN when none exist.
rule_b: For tuples of unequal lengths, return a 'Mean Value' row labelled 'Position i' for each position present in any tuple, averaging only available numeric values and using NaN when none exist.

class: Nonempty lists of equal-length tuples containing at least one finite, non-integer floating-point value.
rule_a: For each position, calculate the mean using only integer values, ignoring floating-point values and strings, and return np.nan if no integers remain.
rule_b: For each position, calculate the mean using integer and floating-point values, ignoring strings, and return np.nan if no numeric values remain.

class: Lists containing at least two consecutive points with identical coordinates.
rule_a: For lists containing consecutive identical points, return Euclidean distances in order for unequal consecutive pairs only, omitting pairs with identical coordinates.
rule_b: For lists containing consecutive identical points, return Euclidean distances in order for every consecutive pair, including 0.0 for pairs with identical coordinates.

class: Student data contains repeated names with different ages.
rule_a: The returned dataframe must sort rows by name ascending and preserve input order within each name regardless of age.
rule_b: The returned dataframe must sort rows by name ascending and order rows within each name by age ascending.

class: Nonempty lists of dictionaries containing finite numeric x, y, and z values, with at least one column constant across all rows.
rule_a: Each constant column must map to 0.5 in every row, while each nonconstant column must be independently scaled using (value − column minimum) / (column maximum − column minimum).
rule_b: Each constant column must map to 0.0 in every row, while each nonconstant column must be independently scaled using (value − column minimum) / (column maximum − column minimum).

class: Lists containing multiple error logs at the same time of day, with at least one error at a different time of day.
class_inputs: (['2021-06-15 09:00:00 ERROR: Connection failed', '2021-06-15 09:00:00 ERROR: Authentication failed', '2021-06-15 12:00:00 ERROR: Backup failed'],)
(['2021-06-15 08:00:00 ERROR: Connection failed', '2021-06-15 08:00:00 ERROR: Authentication failed', '2021-06-15 08:00:00 ERROR: Query failed', '2021-06-15 16:00:00 ERROR: Backup failed'],)
(['2021-06-15 01:00:00 ERROR: Connection failed', '2021-06-15 01:00:00 ERROR: Authentication failed', '2021-06-15 07:00:00 ERROR: Query failed', '2021-06-15 10:00:00 ERROR: Backup failed'],)
(['2021-06-15 09:00:00 ERROR: Connection failed', '2021-06-15 09:00:00 ERROR: Authentication failed', '2021-06-15 15:00:00 ERROR: Query failed', '2021-06-15 15:00:00 ERROR: Backup failed'],)
other_inputs: (['2021-06-15 08:00:00 ERROR: Connection failed', '2021-06-15 12:00:00 ERROR: Backup failed'],)
(['2021-06-15 06:00:00 ERROR: Connection failed', '2021-06-15 09:00:00 WARNING: Low disk space', '2021-06-15 12:00:00 ERROR: Query failed', '2021-06-15 18:00:00 ERROR: Backup failed'],)
rule_a: When error logs share a time of day, the average error time must weight each distinct time of day equally, regardless of its number of occurrences.
rule_b: When error logs share a time of day, the average error time must weight each distinct time of day by its number of occurrences.

class: Lists containing exactly one dictionary with finite numeric values for all three keys 'x', 'y', and 'z'.
rule_a: For a single dictionary containing finite numeric values for 'x', 'y', and 'z', each key's mean, sum, maximum, and minimum must equal its sole value, and its standard deviation must be NaN.
rule_b: For a single dictionary containing finite numeric values for 'x', 'y', and 'z', each key's mean, sum, maximum, and minimum must equal its sole value, and its standard deviation must be zero.

class: Lists containing duplicate letters, repeated a positive number of times.
rule_a: For a list containing duplicate letters and a positive repetition count, return each distinct letter with a frequency equal to the repetition count.
rule_b: For a list containing duplicate letters and a positive repetition count, return each distinct letter with a frequency equal to its number of occurrences in the original list multiplied by the repetition count.

class: Nonempty lists of dictionaries in which at least one of 'x', 'y', and 'z' is absent from every dictionary.
rule_a: For each of 'x', 'y', and 'z', the result must omit the key if it is absent from every input dictionary and otherwise include its value counts as a Counter.
rule_b: For each of 'x', 'y', and 'z', the result must include the key with an empty Counter if it is absent from every input dictionary and otherwise include its value counts as a Counter.

class: DataFrames with multiple text columns in which both the specified column and another text column contain English stopwords.
class_inputs: (pd.DataFrame({'text': ['this is music', 'birds can fly'], 'notes': ['the first song', 'our small nest']}), 'text')
(pd.DataFrame({'id': [7], 'summary': ['it is sunny'], 'details': ['we walk outside'], 'label': ['a good day']}), 'summary')
rule_a: For a DataFrame with multiple text columns, remove English stopwords from every text column, preserving non-text columns.
rule_b: For a DataFrame with multiple text columns, remove English stopwords only from the specified column, preserving all other columns.

class: Words containing both uppercase and lowercase ASCII letters.
rule_a: For words containing both uppercase and lowercase ASCII letters, convert the word to lowercase, compute each adjacent difference as the next letter's ASCII value minus the current letter's ASCII value, and calculate entropy from the resulting array.
rule_b: For words containing both uppercase and lowercase ASCII letters, preserve the word's original casing, compute each adjacent difference as the next letter's ASCII value minus the current letter's ASCII value, and calculate entropy from the resulting array.

class: Lowercase alphabetic strings containing a run of at least three identical letters, so a repeated-letter pair has overlapping occurrences.
rule_a: For such strings, the returned dictionary must contain all 676 lowercase two-letter keys, with each value equal to the maximum number of non-overlapping occurrences of that pair in the string, or zero if absent.
rule_b: For such strings, the returned dictionary must contain all 676 lowercase two-letter keys, with each value equal to the total number of occurrences of that pair in the string, including overlapping occurrences, or zero if absent.

class: ASCII strings containing at least one uppercase letter and at least two letters in total.
rule_a: For these strings, remove nonalphabetic characters, convert all remaining letters to lowercase, and count every overlapping adjacent two-letter combination.
rule_b: For these strings, remove nonalphabetic characters, preserve the original case of all remaining letters, and count every overlapping adjacent two-letter combination.

class: ASCII strings containing at least one digit, optionally mixed with letters, spaces, or punctuation.
rule_a: For ASCII strings containing digits, count only letters after removing digits and punctuation or whitespace, combining uppercase and lowercase forms under lowercase keys.
rule_b: For ASCII strings containing digits, count both letters and digits after removing punctuation or whitespace, combining uppercase and lowercase letter forms under lowercase keys.

class: Strings containing adjacent two-letter combinations that recur with different capitalization after non-alphabetic characters are removed.
rule_a: The most frequent adjacent two-letter combination must be selected using separate counts for different capitalizations, and the returned combination must be lowercased.
rule_b: The most frequent adjacent two-letter combination must be selected using combined counts across different capitalizations, and the returned combination must be lowercased.

class: Nonempty strings consisting solely of English letters and containing at least one uppercase letter.
rule_a: For a nonempty string consisting solely of English letters with at least one uppercase letter, convert it to lowercase and return a DataFrame with one row per character in order, using columns 'Letter' and 'Position' with 1-based English alphabet positions.
rule_b: For a nonempty string consisting solely of English letters with at least one uppercase letter, raise ValueError.

class: DataFrames whose 'text' values are ASCII strings containing underscores.
rule_a: For ASCII strings containing underscores, cleaning must retain letters, digits, and underscores, remove all other characters, and report the length of the resulting string.
rule_b: For ASCII strings containing underscores, cleaning must retain letters and digits, remove all other characters including underscores, and report the length of the resulting string.

class: Strings containing a non-whitespace line with two or more consecutive tab characters.
rule_a: Exclude whitespace-only lines, preserve the order and all other characters of retained lines, and replace each maximal run of consecutive tabs with one space in the 'Text' column.
rule_b: Exclude whitespace-only lines, preserve the order and all other characters of retained lines, and replace each individual tab with one space in the 'Text' column.

class: Numeric DataFrames without NaN values whose columns have nonmonotonic cumulative sums with distinct first and last cumulative values.
rule_a: For each such column, normalize each cumulative value by subtracting the column's first cumulative value and dividing by its last cumulative value minus its first cumulative value.
rule_b: For each such column, normalize each cumulative value by subtracting the column's minimum cumulative value and dividing by its maximum cumulative value minus its minimum cumulative value.

class: Nonempty animal and food lists with distinct animal names and repeated food names.
rule_a: For these inputs, the DataFrame must contain one row per animal and one column per distinct food name, with each cell containing the corresponding 'animal:food' string.
rule_b: For these inputs, the DataFrame must contain one row per animal and one column per food-list occurrence, with each cell containing the corresponding 'animal:food' string.

class: Input lists containing repeated identical numeric-value/category tuples.
rule_a: Repeated identical tuples must contribute only once each to both the numeric sum and the category counts.
rule_b: Repeated identical tuples must contribute once per occurrence to both the numeric sum and the category counts.

class: Supplied datasets whose area strings are not in ascending numeric order.
rule_a: For these datasets, the prediction must use a linear regression fitted after independently sorting the numeric areas and prices into ascending order.
rule_b: For these datasets, the prediction must use a linear regression fitted with each numeric area paired with its corresponding price in the supplied dataset.

class: Valid dictionaries containing exactly one score string and one corresponding grade.
rule_a: For input containing exactly one score–grade pair, raise ValueError because Pearson correlation requires at least two observations.
rule_b: For input containing exactly one score–grade pair, return NaN because Pearson correlation requires at least two observations.

class: Text containing HTTP or HTTPS URLs whose paths or query strings contain words.
rule_a: For URLs with paths or query strings, remove only the scheme and host, leaving words in the path and query string eligible for counting alongside words outside URLs.
rule_b: For URLs with paths or query strings, remove the entire URL, leaving only words outside URLs eligible for counting.

class: Texts containing capitalized or mixed-case versions of predefined stopwords outside URLs.
class_inputs: ('They were WITH us before THE show',)
other_inputs: ('we are here and we are ready',)
rule_a: After removing URLs, words must be matched against the predefined stopwords case-insensitively and counted under their lowercase forms.
rule_b: After removing URLs, words must be matched against the predefined stopwords case-sensitively and counted only when their original forms match.

class: Collections containing at least one document consisting solely of HTTP or HTTPS URLs and whitespace, alongside at least one document containing ordinary words.
rule_a: After removing URLs, discard documents left empty, exclude them from the document count used for TF-IDF, and return score tuples only for the remaining documents in their original order.
rule_b: After removing URLs, retain documents left empty, include them in the document count used for TF-IDF, and return an all-zero score tuple for each at its original position.

class: Lists containing at least one dictionary in which multiple URL keys have the same value.
rule_a: When multiple URL keys in one dictionary share a value, those keys must collectively contribute one occurrence to that value's frequency when selecting and reporting the most common value.
rule_b: When multiple URL keys in one dictionary share a value, each key must separately contribute one occurrence to that value's frequency when selecting and reporting the most common value.

class: Dictionaries in which at least one word is paired with a letter that occurs in that word but is not its first letter.
rule_a: Count every letter occurrence in each word whose first letter matches its associated value, excluding words whose first letter does not match.
rule_b: Count every letter occurrence in each word, including words whose first letter does not match their associated value.
